updates.title: Keeping texture alpha before presentation conversion
updates.summary: The reader now exposes raw palette alpha separately from viewer transparency. A read-only check on the three retail candidates confirms why converted alpha cannot be reused as GPU test data.
changes: Added distinct raw TIM2/TIM3 images and explicit consuming presentation conversion; existing viewer image semantics and defaults stay unchanged.
Connected original synthetic encoded TIM2/CSM1 data to the ordered GPU component through the raw type.
Added a bounded no-extraction alpha inspector for exact caller-selected ISO room banks. No runtime state or scene visibility is assigned from texture contents.
updates.validation: 72 distinct Rust and25 Python synthetic tests pass. All158 bank images /1,894,912 texels pass raw-to-presentation compatibility checks; original ISO SHA-256 unchanged. Actual Vulkan conformance:4,718,592 exhaustive alpha-stage pixel cases plus573,442 spatial samples; fixtures contain no game data.
updates.limits: 19,980 texels change the unmodulated >127 predicate if presentation alpha is mistaken for raw alpha; this is a diagnostic input difference, not a count of incorrect screen pixels. No blending, production GPU integration or new retail Reference / Bevy pair. Sky activation and full-resource rendering remain open.

link.label: Raw-alpha contract and bounded retail findings

updates.title: Testing separate alpha and depth writes on the GPU
updates.summary: Development resumed after the repository rename. An original offscreen Rust/WGSL component now checks alpha comparisons and independent RGB, stored-alpha and depth writes. It is not a retail renderer fix.
changes: Added a reusable app-library component with caller-ordered draws and complementary passing/failing branches, driven by the existing CPU permission model.
Kept framebuffer alpha as separate data; zero stored alpha does not make the presented RGB transparent.
Added an opt-in no-window, no-disc conformance executable. Production materials and the existing retail screenshots are unchanged.
updates.validation: 67 distinct Rust and25 Python synthetic tests pass. Actual RTX 5080 / Vulkan run:4,718,592 exhaustive pixel cases plus573,442 spatial samples match CPU RGB, stored alpha and depth. Covers all byte-alpha/reference pairs, comparisons, failure actions, depth masks, disabled tests, later occlusion, equal depth, ordering (including overlapping mixed-outcome primitives within one draw), modulation, interpolation and clipping. CI compiles the component and runs CPU tests only.
updates.limits: No blending, fog, lighting, runtime material mapping or retail replay in this component. The current normalized texture alpha is not valid raw input. No new Reference / Bevy pair is manufactured for synthetic GPU work. Sky overpainting, scene activation and gameplay remain open.

link.label: GPU contract, results and remaining integration work

updates.title: Repository renamed to god-hand-rs
updates.summary: The public repository and journal now use the god-hand-rs address. The native-rendering development goal is paused at the owner’s request.
changes: Renamed the existing repository without creating a replacement; updated origin and current repository/Pages links.
Preserved commits, source packages, comparison originals and the local workspace directory.
updates.validation: Verified the public repository identity, admin access and main:/docs Pages configuration. Publication guard and dashboard checks are run for this documentation-only change; no local Rust retest is needed because engine code is unchanged.
updates.limits: This is a repository rename, not new engine functionality. Historical screenshots retain their original pixels and may show the former address. Native-rendering work remains paused.

updates.title: Starting the native rendering goal: separate alpha and depth
updates.summary: The new autonomous goal targets the full-resource sky failure. A rejected all-opaque control restores geometry but breaks other surfaces; the first original CPU model separates alpha-stage write permissions.
changes: Recorded the resumable autonomous workflow and remaining GPU/reference acceptance gates.
Compared a private copy of our app with only its host alpha modes forced opaque, at both unchanged full-resource poses. No production visual change was shipped.
Joined existing geometry-consistent UV candidates to observed draw states; kept raw traces and per-buffer mappings private.
Implemented original GPU-free byte-alpha comparisons and separate RGB, framebuffer-alpha and depth permissions, including failure actions and depth masks.
updates.validation: 64 distinct Rust tests (61 base plus3 viewer-only),25 Python tests and locked Bevy check pass. Alpha/reference pairs are exhaustively checked against an independent three-way truth table, with all failure actions and127/128 boundary coverage. The two private ten-second native Vulkan controls exit normally and use the public lockfile registry versions/checksums.
updates.limits: CPU model only: not wired into Bevy yet. All-opaque is a negative control, not a renderer or scene-activation fix. It changes blending/queue selection as well as depth behavior; cutouts, shadows and sky regress. Per-draw assignment, GPU tests, exact GS-vs-host blend arithmetic, full rendering and gameplay remain unfinished.

updates.title: Checking a second retail viewpoint
updates.summary: The existing engine places the same retail resources consistently after the reference camera has turned and moved. No mesh or transform was adjusted for the new view.
changes: Resumed an existing retail state recorded after analog movement and attack-button inputs, preserving the prototype as a separate reference.
Repeated passive trace/control validation and estimated one projection with four whole resources held out.
Rendered and repeated the new view using the already published engine revision. Geometry and source transforms are unchanged.
Retained failed full-resource renders: sky layers still overpaint the street, so scene activation and render state remain unresolved.
updates.validation: 60 distinct Rust /25 Python synthetic tests and locked build/check pass. The three retail candidates remain readable. All147 held-out UV-candidate points are within1px of the common fit (median0.0255px); omitted or0.01-scaled translations give0/147. These are geometric observation checks, not image-fidelity scores. New traced/control native frame and Bevy replay are byte-identical.
updates.limits: 19 candidate resources, all unit-scale/zero-rotation; only four are held out. An inherited private reporting label counted an absent saloon id as a fifth resource; corrected before publication, with point counts/residuals unchanged. No general Euler order, complete rendering, camera-motion behavior or gameplay is claimed. Sky, actors/HUD and full material/light/fog/alpha/filter/pass state remain missing or wrong.

updates.title: One projection for several street landmarks
updates.summary: Passive vertex observations give a shared inspection pose across near and distant static resources. The street renders without moving individual objects; camera behavior and the renderer are still incomplete.
changes: Compared bounded source UV candidates to passive GS output, with a common projective fit and whole resources withheld.
Separated projection aspect from framebuffer dimensions; added explicit back-face culling after a rear surface blocked the first two-sided render.
Captured the real street without moving objects. Retained every earlier comparison and the failed originals locally.
Added CPU/Bevy matrix and resize tests; free public CI also runs viewer-only synthetic tests without a disc or GPU.
updates.validation: 57 base Rust tests plus 3 additional viewer-only tests, 25 Python tests, fmt, locked build/check and five pre-ISO CLI error cases pass. A shared fit predicts 862/865 held-out candidate points within one pixel (median 0.024 px); this is geometric observation consistency, not image fidelity. Traced/control native output and new workflow replay remain byte-identical; default/off output is preserved.
updates.limits: Only one snapshot and unit-scale/zero-rotation matched resources. No general Euler order, camera motion, complete rendering or game logic. The first two-sided render was occluded; a texture-mirror identity test failed and was not used. Sky, actors/HUD, some props and exact lighting/fog/alpha/filter/passes remain missing or wrong.

updates.title: Reading source colors, not yet full game lighting
updates.summary: The viewer can now read the mesh color stream and use an explicit modulation experiment. The camera stays fixed; some facades darken, but shadow regions expose remaining rendering errors.
changes: Confirmed the complete r100 geometry/texture SCP span is present unchanged in the reference snapshot; the whole surrounding DAT is not byte-identical.
Observed the native backend’s existing draw trace without changing its code. A traced/control newly rendered frame pair remained byte-identical.
Preserved raw source colors in the bounded MDB reader and added an original embedded modulation shader, disabled by default.
Published the actual opt-in result alongside the reference; retained the earlier default-mode capture for before/after comparison.
updates.validation: 56 Rust and 25 Python synthetic tests pass. Two private no-disc GPU probes match seven expected RGB samples exactly, including a depth-varying triangle that distinguishes screen-linear interpolation. The harness uses registry versions/checksums from the public Cargo.lock. The real scene mode and scripted replay captured identical PNGs; default mode still matches its earlier PNG.
updates.limits: This is not complete GS lighting or a quality score. Source colors differ from final lit draw colors; fog, filtering, alpha state and multiple passes remain unresolved. Some shadows are too dark. Reference draw observations were from nearby frames, not an exact draw map for the published frame. No game code or original instructions were used.

updates.title: A reproducible street-level comparison
updates.summary: The yellow saloon sign now gives us an identifiable static landmark in both the retail reference and Bevy. This is a manually fitted comparison camera, not original camera behavior.
changes: Added explicit inspection eye/target/FOV and physical viewport parameters, plus GPU-free projection tests.
Identified the saloon sign through its actual material-to-mesh association; kept texture inspection extracts private.
Preserved failed rear-facing and occluded trials, then captured a street-level view at 512 × 448 without cropping or retouching.
Published a new same-landmark pair while retaining the earlier unmatched overview and all original files.
updates.validation: 52 synthetic Rust tests and 24 Python tests pass; formatting and viewer compilation pass. Four linked Windows/Vulkan camera runs captured original PNGs and exited at their 10-second limits. Invalid, incomplete, nonfinite and oversized camera/viewport inputs were rejected before opening a disc. A fifth run through the scripted workflow repeated the final pose with byte-identical PNG output on this setup.
updates.limits: The camera was manually fitted around one facade. Neighboring-wall parallax, colors, shadows, sky and actors still differ. Original game camera, complete scene activation and general transform/material parity remain unverified. No image-quality percentage or gameplay result is claimed.

updates.title: Placing real retail resources — diagnostic only
updates.summary: The Bevy viewer can now assemble a candidate town layout from the ISO. The first reference/Bevy pair is published in the comparison section, explicitly unmatched: gameplay camera versus overhead inspection.
changes: Specified and tested six explicit affine rotation sequences; multiaxis nodes without an order are refused, not guessed.
Reproduced all geometry counts on three retail candidates. An explicit r100 subset renders 148 nodes and 23,288 triangles.
Rejected an occluded desktop capture, then added direct framebuffer PNG capture. The all-resource view exposed a sky-rendering problem; manual exclusions remain clearly logged.
Recaptured the first-fight reference without a window. Published its unchanged PPM with a lossless PNG preview, alongside the original Bevy PNG.
updates.validation: 48 synthetic Rust tests and 24 Python tests pass. The linked Windows/Vulkan viewer saved its own framebuffer and exited normally after 30 seconds. The reference run exited normally at its planned frame limit; local comparison verified that the PNG preview preserves every original PPM RGB sample.
updates.limits: This is not a playable scene or a fidelity pass. Camera/scene alignment is unmatched, sky/material state is unresolved, and diagnostic exclusions are not game visibility rules. Rotation composition and units remain hypotheses. No actors, HUD, collision or gameplay are implemented.
